title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 79-80
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 79 to 80 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'सुवर्णवर्णो हेमाङ्गो वराङ्गश्चन्दनाङ्गदी'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 79 to 80 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 79 to 80.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 79 to 80** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **सुवर्णवर्णो हेमाङ्गो वराङ्गश्चन्दनाङ्गदी**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**सुवर्णवर्णो हेमाङ्गो वराङ्गश्चन्दनाङ्गदी । वीरहा विषमः शून्यो घृताशीरचलश्चलः ॥** **अमानी मानदो मान्यो लोकस्वामी त्रिलोकधृक् । सुमेधा मेधजो धन्यः सत्यमेधा धराधरः ॥**

Golden in hue, golden of limb, noble of form is he. Anointed with sandal and wearing armlets, he is that God of gods. The slayer of foes, matchless, the void, pure as ghee, both the unmoving and the moving. Free of pride, he gives honour to others and is worthy of honour himself. The master of the worlds who carries all three is that God of gods. Of fine intellect, the giver of wisdom, blessed, true of mind, the bearer of the earth.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 79 to 80 mean?
faq.a: Golden in hue, golden of limb, noble of form is he. Anointed with sandal and wearing armlets, he is that God of gods. The slayer of foes, matchless, the void, pure as ghee, both the unmoving and the moving. Free of pride, he gives honour to others and is worthy of honour himself. The master of the worlds who carries all three is that God of gods. Of fine intellect, the giver of wisdom, blessed, true of mind, the bearer of the earth.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
